title: Elephant Therianthrope
paragraphs: What kind of “dragon” or “divine dragon” is that? Just thinking about it makes me furious. That politician… should I tear him to pieces?
“Father, why are you just taking that kind of outrageous nonsense at face value!?”

“That man is probably a decent person. The strength of the Spear Hero… He must have known what kind of person Motoyasu-kun is, yet he still voiced his opinion. He must have been prepared to die for the country.”
Father, you’re actually speaking highly of that dragon-pushing guy from earlier! That’s a huge mistake! Dragons are just good at sucking up to those in power.
“Besides, he came forward with concrete proposals for improvement when things had gotten this bad.”
“If things are this much of a hassle, shouldn’t we just leave Shieldfreeden alone?”

To be blunt, there’s absolutely no reason for Father to take care of Shieldfreeden. I know the situation is dire due to Takt’s exploitation, but he shouldn’t have the luxury of even saying such a thing.
“……I think if we just leave things as they are, it’ll turn into an even bigger headache.”
“Is that so?”

“There’s a massive divide between the wealthy and the lower classes in Shieldfreeden. Until now, Takt has been keeping everyone in the dark by showing them a happy dream, but that’s gone. In other words, we’re on the brink of a riot.”

Happy dreams… As long as Takt is around, things probably seem to be running smoothly. However, since resources are limited, it’s impossible to satisfy everyone. There will always be a certain number of people who gain and those who lose out. In reality, the system was kept afloat by shifting the burden onto someone—someone hidden from view. Those people are the lower classes.

If a riot breaks out among the lower classes, we’ll be facing not only the situation where we have to pay massive reparations due to our defeat, but also civil unrest. I don’t think the civil unrest itself is such a big problem, but the chaos caused by it would be a convenient situation for Takt’s remnants.
“Even so! We don’t need any dragons!”

“But if things stay this way, there’ll still be a certain number of people willing to harbor the remnants of the Takt faction—even if their entire clan faces punishment for doing so. Those guys have enough money and connections to keep their opponents quiet. Even without that, they’re the kind of people driven by religious fervor, so I’d prefer to keep them in check if possible…”

Ugh… I never imagined that letting him slip away back then would lead to such a huge mess. This is just too much, no matter how you look at it. For that total nobody, Takt, to leave behind such a troublesome problem—I wish he’d just cut it out already!
“The fact that he’s hoarded money and has all sorts of connections behind the scenes makes this incredibly troublesome…”

“Takt is a reincarnated being… Unlike us, he’s been active for years, so the difference in raw ability is showing. And since he was covering up the problems himself, they’re all coming to a head now that he’s gone. This pattern matches the characteristics of reincarnated beings that Motoyasu-kun mentioned.”

…Reincarnated individuals must have been erasing the traces they left behind in this manner. I suppose you could say it’s a situation that can’t hold together without the person himself? Since Takt has vanished, Shieldfreeden will inevitably collapse—both in the original world and in this one.

“I never imagined that people driven by a desire for revenge would be such a hassle… There must be more they could do… But then again, since they were content with the benefits and status they gained from Takt, I suppose it’s only natural.”

I remember that Father was deeply troubled by that very thing when he came to Siltvelt. This might sound harsh, but this world is essentially a loop back to the initial world. Therefore, it’s a loop with very little information. Since I couldn’t provide much information either, Father didn’t have many options. That’s probably why we’re in this situation.
“All we have to do is exterminate every last one of those swine’s relatives!”
“We’re already doing that on a global scale. But even those factions are lying low, biding their time. Even with the power of Faubrey and Siltvelt… we can’t exterminate every last one of them.”

Ah, I’m painfully aware of just how much easier it was in the first world—and in the worlds where we were able to swiftly dispose of Takt up until now. It’s infuriating to see those vermin-like creatures multiplying. If they organized into an army and came swarming at me, I’d wipe them out myself.
“Well… I don’t think there are that many clever people around here, even within the Takt faction, but letting those guys slip away was a real blow.”
“So, is Father going to raise a dragon to pay for that!?”
“If Motoyasu-kun doesn’t want to do it, I guess I’ll just have to do it myself.”
“I don’t want Father to raise one either!”

Not a single one of these dragons is any good. A self-proclaimed “weakest” who’s strangely pathetic, a pervert who wants a sex change, and a needlessly carnivorous sycophant! Not to mention the misguided Takt supremacists. …Even setting my personal feelings aside, aren’t there really no decent ones among them? What’s the point of increasing the ranks of such people!?
“You’re such a spoiled brat, Spear Hero… Isn’t it just a matter of raising a single dragon?”
“I’m not being spoiled! Sakura-chan isn’t happy about it either! Even Filo-tan hates the idea!”

Philo-tan was always fighting with those dragons. No matter what happens, I can’t possibly let Father raise a dragon under these circumstances. In the loops so far, he only reluctantly agreed because he judged that we had to do it to overcome the crisis! Now that we know we’ve already overcome the crisis and peace will come, they’re just unnecessary people.
“Motoyasu-kun, calm down.”
“I can’t calm down! We can protect the world without any dragons, and without breaking through the level cap!”
“Breaking through the level cap…? Come to think of it, if we use the core of Takt’s dragon, we can perform the ritual to break through the level cap, right?”

Oh no! Father has caught on to the “breaking the level cap” idea he’d tucked away in the back of his mind! He must have completely forgotten about it, what with being so busy with post-war cleanup and the Shieldfreeden issue. In the last loop, I managed to get by by manipulating his perception that it wasn’t necessary, but here I’ve made another huge blunder. But! I’m not an idiot, you know!
“We can manage just fine even without it!”
“Come to think of it, Motoyasu… before we entered this loop, you mentioned there was a troublesome dragon that had started tagging along on the loops, didn’t you?”

Ugh… When I returned to this loop, overcome with emotion, I ended up telling Father a few things—albeit only a little. After all, I’d been taught before that gathering intelligence on the enemy is crucial. I was simply putting that advice into practice.
“F-Father?”
Before long, Father lowered his gaze and began to ponder deeply. I get the feeling that the anger he’d been showing just a moment ago is quickly fading away.
Motoyasu, you’ve made a fatal mistake, haven’t you?

I felt as if I could hear my own voice saying that. I-it’s all right. No matter what Father says, I won’t listen to him. Dragons are nothing but a nuisance, after all. Since the previous loop proved that, it’s an unshakable truth.
“Hmm… if we go this way…”
Just as Father muttered that, he looked up.
“Looks like you’ve got a good idea. It’ll be interesting to see if you can convince the Spear Hero.”
“I suppose so.”
“Even if it comes from you, Father, I cannot approve of raising a dragon.”
“Calm down, Motoyasu. Try looking at it from a different perspective.”
No matter how I look at it, my conviction won’t waver. Through my countless loop experiences, I’ve observed dragons from every angle. As a result, I’ve concluded that dragons are the enemy.
“The dragon Motoyasu-kun was talking about—it loops just like Motoyasu-kun does… I’m pretty sure it stores its memories inside a spear and transfers itself that way, right?”
“That’s right. What’s your point?”
“Think about it carefully, Motoyasu. What’s troubling you about being in this world? The Sakura-chan who’s already here is actually Filo-chan in another world, isn’t she?”
……? Why are we talking about Filo-chan and Sakura-chan when we’re discussing dragons?
“Y-yes, that’s right.”

Faced with Father’s persuasion… I feel a cold sweat running down my spine. My wild instincts, honed alongside Lady Filolial, are telling me: That I cannot win against Father’s persuasion. I’ll definitely refuse!

“Then… if I can persuade that dragon and understand the method, even if it’s impossible in this world, when I become Sakura-chan in future loop worlds, wouldn’t she pass on her memories to the girl named Filo?”
“What!? Does that mean Filo-tan and I will be together forever!?”
Guh!? Motoyasu—the part of me dedicated to “Dragon Extermination”—collapsed after taking a punch from Father!?
“U-uh, you must not accept that. Such a proposal… it’s bound to fail.”
Dragon-Exterminating Motoyasu! Don’t get back up! Here, Motoyasu, driven by his love for Filo-chan, approaches Dragon-Exterminating Motoyasu.
“It’s all for the sake of achieving true peace with Filo-chan! For that reason, we must accept this momentary pain!”
With a thud, the Motoyasu who loves Filo-chan stomped on Dragon-Hunting Motoyasu and delivered a follow-up blow. Then, straddling him, he locked Dragon-Hunting Motoyasu in a reverse crab hold.
“Guaaaaaaaaaa—What are you doing?! You should be ashamed of yourself for using a dragon’s power! You lot will absolutely regret this! I’ll curse you allllllll!”
Clang, clang, clang! In my mind, the victor’s chant and the cheers of countless Motoyasus erupt. Then, just like in a hero interview, Motoyasu—who loves Filo-tan—took the mic and made a proposal.

“There’s no need to exploit Rival Dragons to find a new Dragon… There are exceptions to every rule. As frustrating as it is, there is a Dragon who has actually managed to get along with Filolial-sama.”
W-why are you bringing up such a taboo subject here!? Weren’t you supposed to be Motoyasu, the one who loves Filo-tan? However, it’s a fact that such a situation did exist in the past.

“We just need to make that child the Dragon Emperor. Once they become the Dragon Emperor, their stats will surely be the same. We can have them analyze the spear and use the space that Rival was using.”
Oh! That’s a brilliant idea! Forever! It’s the Eternal Filo-tan Plan! The birth of the strongest Filo-tan the entire world—and every loop—has ever hoped for!
“That’s a brilliant idea! We absolutely must do this!”

Father nodded gently at my words. As expected of Father—I’m glad I consulted with him. Now that I have a concrete plan to solve the problems within the loop, I know exactly what I need to do. Wooohooo, I’m going to give it my all!
“Hmm… this is impressive. You’ve really gotten the hang of handling the Spear Hero, haven’t you?”
“Well, I’ve gotten pretty used to it by now. I figured you’d agree to this proposal.”
Even I would change my mind if I heard Father’s brilliant idea. His suggestion was just that compelling.
“But Father, I’ll be the one to carefully select which dragon we raise.”
“As long as Motoyasu-kun’s satisfied, that’s fine by me. Well then, let’s head back to Siltvelt and retrieve the Dragon Emperor’s Core that’s been stored in the warehouse.”

And so, with our course of action decided, we returned to the meeting with the people of Shieldfreeden, where it was decided that we would accept the proposal. And so… we used a portal to return to Siltvelt right then and there. In the blink of an eye, we arrived at Siltvelt Castle!
The Shusaku representative and the elderly Genmu representative, who had returned ahead of us, welcomed us.
“—So, to boost our approval ratings in Shieldfreeden, we’ve decided to start raising dragons.”
“What a pitiful lot…”
“Don’t say that. This is a nation founded by those who could never fit in at Siltvelt to begin with. It was only to be expected that their faith in the Shield Hero would be lacking.”
Each representative replied. Naturally, their reactions toward the people of Shieldfreeden were rather contemptuous.

“After all, wasn’t it our own excessive devotion that ended up causing trouble for the Shield Hero? Perhaps believers like those in Shieldfreeden would have been better suited to support the Heroes’ efforts. Of course, that’s excluding ambitious individuals like Takt’s faction.”
“But…”
“In time, we’ll simply guide the people of Shieldfreeden to worship the Shield Hero through the Dragon. Just think of this as the beginning of a new history.”

That’s right. Father is educating the people of Shieldfreeden. In other words, I, too, am standing at the beginning of a new history where I can loop with Filo-chan. What a truly heartwarming turn of events. Lord Filolial looping… Let’s name this year the First Year of Loop Filolial.
“…Understood.”
The representative of the Shusaku clan took a step back.
“Then I shall present the Core Stones stored in the castle’s treasury.”

Saying that, he gave orders to the soldiers, sending them to retrieve the Core Stones requested by Father. If I think of them as the materials needed to loop with Filo-tan, my aversion to the Dragon Emperor’s Core Stones lessens somewhat. Once we have some spare time, we should gather a few more.
“Well, in the meantime…”

Exuding a strange aura, the two representatives of the Siltvelt species flashed suspicious smiles. Father was looking at them both with a puzzled expression. These guys… what on earth are they planning to do?
“Bring her here…”
“She’s already waiting.”
“Then go fetch her.”

Following that exchange, accompanied by somewhat heavy footsteps, a therianthrope entered the throne room from the front. That fellow… is a large elephant therianthrope. Dressed in an ornate knight’s outfit, he approached Father—who had been seated on the throne—and crouched down to salute him.
“Oh?”
At this point, Panda blinked several times at the therianthrope and spoke up. Father tilted his head toward the two representatives, furrowing his brow.
“This is Elmero-Puhant. She belongs to one of the most powerful families in Siltvelt and has been traveling the world to broaden her horizons.”
“That’s one way of putting it… She’s not some so-called ‘prodigal knight’ who’s been wandering the lands as she pleased just because she couldn’t inherit the family estate, is she?”

As Panda said that, the therianthrope glared sharply at him. But it was only for a moment; he then turned his gaze to Father and continued to stand at attention, looking tense. Father looked at Panda and gave him a signal, as if to ask, “Do you know him?” Panda nodded.

“Back in the day, when I was testing my strength in Zeltoble, I met him briefly. As far as combat goes… as far as I know, he ranks within the top five, excluding those under the Hero’s protection and the Takt faction.”
“Huh… So, why is someone like that here?”
“After the recent upheaval, she was dispatched to the Faubrey area, where she played a key role in capturing Nana Alsaholn Faubrey, a key figure among the remnants of the Takt faction.”
That name sounds familiar.
